findings.evidence: Step 1.5 and Step 5 repeat the same merge, partial-status and round-log conditions several times (lines 361, 373, 380, 387-391, 465)
findings.fix: Keep one statement of when merge-reports runs and what it binds in Step 1.5, and replace the repeats with a link to references/lane-failure.md#partial-status. Record each removed sentence in docs/audit/recovery/ai-kit-spec-review/record.md.

findings.evidence: The Process-pattern loop runs to 498 lines, and Steps 1 and 4 pack several branches into single paragraphs (lines 346, 426)
findings.fix: Split the line-426 classify paragraph into a numbered sub-procedure (classify, re-pass, branch on Status), and keep the Process pattern's phase-and-checkpoint shape.

findings.evidence: '## NEVER (hard landmines)' lists only two items. The rest sit in the Hard rules table, and several landmines stay inline (never render the dispatch command yourself, never drop a refused --files path, never review inline without a subagent tool)
findings.fix: Add the inline landmines to the NEVER section with their one-line reasons: never hand-render the dispatch-reviewer argv, never drop a refused --files path, never review inline when the host has no fresh-context tool, never pass a non-alias model to the Agent tool. Link each one to the step that owns it.

findings.evidence: The description spends most of its 831 characters on internal mechanics ('orchestrates a clean-context reviewer ... routes fixes via the appropriate handler (native framework skill, slash command, or direct-edit fixer)') and too little on user intent such as 'is this doc ready to hand off'
findings.fix: Use when a design, spec, requirements, RFC or plan document needs review, or review-and-fix, before the next step, including when the user asks whether a doc is ready to build or hand off, or what they would regret building as written. Works across superpowers, GSD, OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD and generic docs. It reviews the doc in a clean context, grounded in the doc's own worktree and lifecycle stage, and loops review and fix until approved or the iteration cap. Optional cross-AI reviewers via --cross-ai/--no-cross-ai. Triggered by 'ai-kit-spec-review', 'review my spec/plan', or document paths given for review. Not for code, PR or commit review, grading a SKILL.md, executing or writing a plan, or setting up reviewer lanes (ai-kit-spec-config).

findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 498 lines, at the 500-line limit and over about 5000 tokens. Every run loads the Step 1 subprocess exit handling (lines 302-355) and the Step 5 outcome table (lines 444-465), even on --no-cross-ai or native-only runs
findings.fix: Move the subprocess-route detail (lines 308-351) into references/cross-ai-dispatch.md#step-1-subprocess-dispatch and gate it with 'Read when an entry's route is subprocess, unverified or custom'. Keep the native route and the two hard rules inline.

findings.evidence: 'a cached profile for a known-to-drift framework (bmad, gsd) older than ~180 days is a refresh candidate — you may re-research and rewrite the cache copy'
findings.fix: Set a default: refresh only when the user asks or when the cached profile's doc_types glob matches no document, and otherwise use the cached copy and mention its age in the Surface message.

findings.evidence: The should-not-trigger near-misses are terse, with no file paths or personal context (for example 'Review my pull request diff for bugs before I merge it into main.')
findings.fix: Rewrite three or four negatives with realistic context, such as a PR number with a diff path, or a SKILL.md path for the grading near-miss, so the boundary is tested on realistic phrasings.

findings.evidence: 'Today only Claude Code selects a model per call (its sonnet, opus, haiku and fable aliases)'. This is a version-sensitive vendor fact with no source URL, no date checked and no live read. Line 294 repeats it as the only valid alias set
findings.fix: Add the official Claude Code subagent documentation URL and the date checked next to the alias list, or read the allowed aliases live from the runner facts that dispatch already uses.

findings.evidence: 'The merge-reports call runs when REVIEWER_LIST has 2 entries'. After ping-lanes or switch-lane rewrites reviewers.json, it is unclear whether the count comes from the original roster or the re-read one
findings.fix: State that the count comes from the reviewers.json re-read after the last ping-lanes or switch-lane call in this iteration.
